<!-- cli-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the CLI; edit the command's help in the code, not this block -->

Run the mutation suites declared in anchors.yaml and ingest the reports.

```text
Runs what the PROJECT declared in `mutation:` and ingests the report.

  anchors mutation                          only the files stale and below the floor, and the never measured
  anchors mutation --all                    every file, through run:
  anchors mutation --budget 10m             fastest first, one file per run, until the time is spent
  anchors mutation unit                     unit only
  anchors mutation unit --target x/y.ts     fills {{target}} in the declared command
  anchors mutation --changed x/y.ts         INCREMENTAL: mutates the impact path
  anchors mutation unit --then check        on passing, charges the gates next

In incremental mode, {{files}} receives only the CODE nodes: mutation alters the rule, and mutating
the test would invert the experiment - the test is the measuring instrument, not the object.

Mutation answers what coverage does not: change the line — does the test notice? A
SURVIVING mutant is a line nobody proves.

Mind the `scope:`: with `isolated` and `full` both ingested, the gate judges by the
ISOLATED one, which is far harsher — it is the one that says whether the unit's test proves the unit,
instead of it being proven by the dependents.
```

## Usage

```bash
anchors mutation [layers...] [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` |  | run every file of the suites through `run:`, whatever their state — the whole run, as before the state selection |
| `--budget` | `0s` | run the files FASTEST FIRST, in batches through `run_changed:`, until this much time is spent (e.g. 60s, 10m); the rest is left for a later run. The order comes from the times recorded by earlier runs; files never timed go last |
| `--changed` |  | INCREMENTAL mode: changed file(s) — runs the `run_changed:` over the union of the impact paths, the same slice as `check --changed` |
| `--include-fresh` |  | also run files measured at the current version that are below the minimum (by default only STALE files below the minimum run) |
| `--include-passing` |  | also run stale files at the minimum or above (by default only files BELOW the minimum run); with --include-fresh, fresh passing files too |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |
| `--scope` |  | filters by the declared SCOPE (`isolated`, `full`) — only on mutation. Without this, runs whichever are declared |
| `--skip-unmeasured` |  | leave out the files never measured (by default they run) |
| `--target` |  | target that replaces `{{target}}` in the declared `run:` (e.g. the file to mutate) |
| `--then` |  | on PASSING, chains Anchors commands: `check`, `coverage` (separate by comma). Opt-in — without this, it runs and stops |
| `-w`, `--workspace` |  | filters by the declared WORKSPACE (backend, mobile…) — repeatable or comma-separated. Combines with the layers: `anchors mutation unit -w backend` |

## The map and its signals — family

Commands of the same family — what tells each apart:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors map`](/docs/cli/commands/map/) | Operate the dependency map (anchors.graph.yaml) |
| [`anchors ingest`](/docs/cli/commands/ingest/) | Ingest test signals (JUnit/lcov) the project generated and bind them to the map |
| [`anchors test`](/docs/cli/commands/test/) | Run the test suites declared in anchors.yaml and ingest the reports |
| **`anchors mutation`** | Run the mutation suites declared in anchors.yaml and ingest the reports |
| [`anchors keep-evidence`](/docs/cli/commands/keep-evidence/) | Declare that a change proves nothing new, keeping the files' evidence fresh |
| [`anchors stamp`](/docs/cli/commands/stamp/) | Write the missing `@contract` stamps on test doubles (never rewrites an existing one) |
| [`anchors recode`](/docs/cli/commands/recode/) | Rename an identity code and propagate it across the project |
| [`anchors renumber`](/docs/cli/commands/renumber/) | Renumber the revisions this branch added when the base already took their number |
| [`anchors generated-paths`](/docs/cli/commands/generated-paths/) | The paths of DERIVED files — whoever conflicts in them rebuilds |
| [`anchors merge-progress`](/docs/cli/commands/merge-progress/) | Progress merge driver: unites both sides, `[x]` beats `[ ]` |
